## Introduction

This vignette shows how to make a model mix by group using the `epiworldR` package. The population is split into groups; agents interact with each other within the same group and with agents from other groups, as a contact matrix says. Any model can mix this way: the groups and the contact matrix are a mixing layer (see `?layer_mixing`) added to it.

## An SEIR model with mixing

For this example, we will simulate an outbreak featuring three populations. The contact matrix is defined as follows:

$$
\left[%
\begin{array}{ccc}
18 & 1 & 1 \\
2 & 16 & 2 \\
2 & 4 & 14 \\
\end{array}%
\right]
$$

This matrix represents the mean number of interactions per day between an agent from population $i$ and an agent from population $j$. The rowsums of the matrix show the mean number of interactions per day for an agent from each population.

The following code chunk defines the group of each agent (three populations of 3,000) and the contact matrix.

```{r}
#| label: entity-matrix-setup
library(epiworldR)

N <- 9e3
groups <- rep(0:2, each = 3e3)

# Row-sums equal to the expected number of interactions
# per day for each agent from each population
cmatrix <- c(
  c(18, 1, 1),
  c(2, 16, 2),
  c(2, 4, 14)
) |> matrix(byrow = TRUE, nrow = 3)
```

With these in hand, we can create the model, an SEIR, and add the mixing layer to it:

```{r}
#| label: model-build
flu_model <- ModelSEIR(
  name              = "Flu",
  n                 = N,
  prevalence        = 1 / N,
  transmission_prob = 0.1,
  latent_period     = 7,
  recovery_rate     = 1 / 7
)

add_layer(
  flu_model,
  layer_mixing("community", groups = groups, contact_matrix = cmatrix)
)
```

Only Infected agents transmit (Exposed agents carry the virus but are not infectious yet), and every agent of a group can be met. The following code-chunk simulates the model for 100 days, summarizes the results, and plots the incidence curve:

```{r}
#| label: model-simulate
set.seed(331)
run(flu_model, ndays = 100)
summary(flu_model)
plot_incidence(flu_model)
```

## Investigating the history

After running the simulation, a possible question is: how many agents from each group were infected each day? The group of each agent is the `groups` vector (agent ids start at 0):

```{r}
#| label: investigate
#| eval: true
library(data.table)

agents_groups <- data.table(agent = seq_len(N) - 1L, group = groups)
head(agents_groups)
```

We can retrieve the daily incidence for each group by merging the transmissions with the agents' groups. The following code chunk accomplishes this:

```{r}
#| label: transmissions
# Retrieving the transmissions
transmissions <- get_transmissions(flu_model) |>
  data.table()

# We only need the date and the source
transmissions <- subset(
  transmissions,
  select = c("date", "source")
)

# Attaching the group to the source
transmissions <- merge(
  transmissions,
  agents_groups,
  by.x = "source", by.y = "agent"
)

# Aggregating by date x group (counts)
transmissions <- transmissions[, .N, by = .(date, group)]

# Taking a look at the data
head(transmissions)
```

With this information, we can now visualize the daily incidence for each group. The following code chunk plots the daily incidence for each group:

```{r}
#| label: transmissions-plot
setorder(transmissions, date, group)

ran <- range(transmissions$N)
transmissions[group == 0, plot(
  x = date, y = N, type = "l", col = "black", ylim = ran)]
transmissions[group == 1, lines(x = date, y = N, col = "red")]
transmissions[group == 2, lines(x = date, y = N, col = "blue")]

legend(
  "topright",
  legend = c("Population 1", "Population 2", "Population 3"),
  col = c("black", "red", "blue"),
  lty = 1
)
```
